method: All four printed pages read from the supplied Part 1 PDF at 2x-5x zoom, with explicit local traversals recorded per page. Ordered source blocks include every instructional bullet, table row/cell, flowchart step, diagram label, arrow annotation and caption. Contiguous labels share an item; consolidation items sit after the lines they test and never pull later material forward. Headers, timestamps, footers and blank Active space excluded.
caveats: p726: the scan prints 'Cardiac arrythmias' and 'afferent arteriole'; questions use standard 'arrhythmias'/'afferent'. 'Tubulo glomerular' is printed as two words; the bank uses TG feedback.

p727: the dehydration chain is taught as printed — increased proximal tubular absorption (+) feeds a macula densa signal of decreased Na+/Cl-/K+ load (higher proximal reabsorption lowers distal delivery). The 'ATI/ATN' slash and the edema rationale for fluid monitoring are source wordings.
p727: JG-cell site 'afferent arteriole > efferent arteriole' is taught as the printed predominance, not an exclusive site.

p728: 'renal artery (end artery)' and '5 segmental arteries (4 anterior + 1 posterior)' are source simplifications taught as printed. The efferent-arteriole 'sandwiched' note is schematic (a vessel between two capillary beds).
p728: 'Urine flows into renal papilla' is taught as printed; standard drainage continues via the minor calyx, which the figure does not label.

p729: the tree arms sum to 90% (85% tubulointerstitial + 5% vascular); glomeruli (10% per the p717 compartment tree) have no arm here. Taught as printed, not completed. The '1. AKI'/'2. CKD' numbering, the m/c cause claims and RTA type 4 as the CKD tubulointerstitial endpoint are source-specific.

pages.traversal: Read top-to-bottom: chapter title; Components list (3 bullets); 'Macula Densa & JG cells' section; MACULA DENSA text (Composition, Site, Function); JG-apparatus figure labels top-to-bottom with caption; 'Applied aspect of TG feedback' header; phases/MOA table row by row, left cell then right cell (row-2 right cell continues onto p727). Lecture timestamp, 'Active space' and footer excluded.

elements.source: Components list: Juxtaglomerular (JG) cells; macula densa; mesangial/lacis/supporting cells/Polkissen cells.
Macula densa composition: modified tall columnar cells.
Macula densa site: cortical portion of thick ascending limb of loop of Henle (TAL)/distal straight tubule.
Macula densa function: tubulo-glomerular (TG) feedback mediated by adenosine.
Composition/site/function of macula densa consolidated as a match, positioned after the three lines.
Macula densa site reconfirmed (true/false), positioned after the figure-independent text.
JG-apparatus figure: efferent arteriole leaving the glomerulus with its smooth muscle layer.
JG-apparatus figure labels: internal elastic lamina (top arteriole wall), glomerular epithelium (tuft covering), basement membrane (tubule wall).
JG-apparatus figure labels: distal tubule (straight) in cross-section, macula densa plaque, JG cells; caption 'JG apparatus'.
Table row 1: phase of tubular injury; duration < 24 hrs.
Row-1 MOA: renal tubular injury from tubulotoxic drugs (eg. gentamicin) leading to PCT injury.
Row-1 MOA: PCT injury lowers reabsorption of solute + H2O, raising their loss in urine.
Row-2 Findings cell as a set: decreased GFR; raised S.creatinine; raised K+ with cardiac arrhythmias (print 'arrythmias'); raised H+ with metabolic acidosis.
Row-2 finding line tested directly: raised H+ leads to metabolic acidosis.
Row-2 MOA: impaired reabsorption of solute + H2O; macula densa senses Cl- > K+ > Na+ load delivered to TAL.
Row-2 MOA: release of adenosine, which constricts the afferent arteriole (print 'afferent'; arrow continues onto p727).

pages.traversal: Table continued: row-2 left cell (Mx) then right cell (MOA chain with its two end branches); row 3 (Recovery phase with dash); B. Dehydration flowchart top-to-bottom including the '+' proximal-absorption input; AKI-causes note (Outside branch complete, then Inside branch); JG Cells (Composition, Site, Function). Header/footer excluded.

elements.source: Row-2 Mx: supportive care; monitor fluid intake because of the raised chance of edema due to renal failure.
Row-2 MOA: afferent constriction lowers GFR (glomerular filtration rate), raising S.creatinine and preventing further salt + H2O loss due to impaired reabsorption.
Row 3: recovery phase with only a dash in the MOA column.
B. Dehydration example (increased vomiting leading to pre-renal failure); first event is loss of intravascular volume.
Dehydration chain: loss of volume lowers glomerular hydrostatic pressure and therefore GFR.
Dehydration chain: increased proximal tubular absorption (+) feeds the macula densa sensing of a decreased Na+/Cl-/K+ load.
Dehydration chain: dilatation of the afferent arteriole, mediated by prostaglandins.
Dehydration chain outcome: GFR rises.
AKI-causes note as a set: outside kidney (pre-renal, post-renal) versus inside kidney (ATI/ATN, acute interstitial nephritis).
AKI cause groups re-tested as a match, positioned after the note.
JG cells composition: granular cells.
JG cells site: tunica media of afferent arteriole more than efferent arteriole (print 'afferent').
JG cells function: produce renin.

pages.traversal: Renin-stimulator diagram (three stimuli left-to-right with (+) arrows into JG cells, then Renin); 'Vascular Anatomy of Kidney' section; renal-circulation chain in forward arrow order; cortex-vs-medulla table (Cortex column top-to-bottom, then Medulla column); vascularity-of-nephron figure (left labels top-to-bottom, right 'sandwiched' annotation, bottom urine caption). Timestamp/footer excluded.

elements.source: Renin stimuli: decreased renal perfusion pressure, prostaglandins and beta-1 receptors all act positively (+) on JG cells, which release renin.
Beta-1 receptor positive drive on JG cells releasing renin.
Beta-1 drive re-tested through a beta-blocker scenario, positioned with the diagram.
Renal circulation starts at the renal artery, labelled an end artery.
Renal artery gives 5 segmental arteries (4 anterior + 1 posterior).
Chain continues: interlobar artery, arcuate artery, interlobular/cortical radial artery.
Afferent arteriole supplies the glomerular capillary plexus in the cortex.
Blood leaves via the efferent arteriole into the peritubular capillary plexus.
Medullary blood supply is mediated by the vasa recta.
Venous return: descending limb to ascending limb of vasa recta, renal vein, IVC (inferior vena cava).
Forward circulation order consolidated (odd-one-out), positioned after the full chain.
Cortex-vs-medulla table: cortex supplied by the renal artery with good supply; medulla supplied by vasa recta with poor supply.
Medulla: pars recta/proximal straight tubule is m/c vulnerable to hypoxia.
Zone-perfusion contrast reconfirmed (true/false), positioned before the figure questions.
Vascularity-figure upper labels: afferent arteriole entering the tuft, proximal convoluted tubule beside the glomerulus, glomerular capsule cupping the tuft.
Vascularity-figure vessel labels: interlobular artery (red) with interlobular vein and its venule (blue).
Vascularity-figure labels as a set: glomerular capsule, peritubular capillary network, loop of the nephron (no macula densa).
Right annotation: efferent arteriole sandwiched between glomerular and peritubular capillary plexuses.
Bottom annotation: urine flows into the renal papilla; caption 'Vascularity of nephron'.

pages.traversal: Note read as a tree: root 'Renal diseases', left branch completed first (85% arm: AKI with the ATN/AIN pair, then CKD with RTA type 4), then right branch (5% arm: large-vessel disease to RAS, small-vessel disease to TMA with hypertensive crisis progressing to CKD). Header/footer excluded.

elements.source: Tree root and left arm: tubules & interstitium form 85% of the kidney.
Left arm 1. AKI (hours to days): ATN due to ischemia (m/c); AIN due to drug hypersensitivity (m/c).
Left arm 2. CKD: chronic tubulointerstitial fibrosis/disease leading to RTA type 4.
Right arm: vascular disease forms 5% of the kidney; large vessel disorders lead to RAS (renal artery stenosis); small vessel disorders lead to TMA (thrombotic microangiopathy).
Small-vessel chain: TMA to hypertensive crisis, progressing to CKD (ischemic nephropathy).
Vascular arm consolidated (true/false), positioned after both branches.
Vascular arm consolidated (odd-one-out), positioned after both branches.
